column1: SE already has the language skill to deliver a pitch — the job here is picking the RIGHT data, not more of it. 'Dehaat Center Ko Jaano' is the heading the SE reads first (opened from the DC Card tab) before any Ask/Tell/Wish. 'Applicable Sources' below is the curated set for that purpose's Win Condition, referencing the 8 sources on the first tab.

column3: Who: Turnover + Repayment Cycle + Scheme Tier (sets billing urgency framing). Where DC Stands / Private Label: not applicable.
column4: What's blocking billing this cycle — stock movement, cash cycle, or a pending dispute? Confirm expected billing date.
column5: Current outstanding; YTD purchase vs. expectation; last year's billing pattern for this period.
column6: A specific date + amount commitment before leaving — not a vague 'soon.'
column7: S5 Outstanding · S6 Last Year DC Purchase · S7 YTD DC Purchase

column3: Who: Repayment Cycle is the key field — flags whether this DC is trending overdue vs. its own norm. Where DC Stands / Private Label: not applicable.
column4: When can we expect payment against the outstanding? Is there a dispute holding it up?
column5: Exact outstanding + aging; this DC's own historical payment behavior for leverage; last year's comparable period.
column6: A firm payment promise (date + amount) — the overdue is actually resolved, not just acknowledged.
column7: S3 Historical Purchase/Sale · S5 Outstanding · S6 Last Year DC Purchase

column3: Who: Business Area Strength gives quick context on what this DC typically stocks. Where DC Stands / Private Label: not applicable — purely operational.
column4: What exactly is the issue — sync, delivery, invoice mismatch, portal access?
column5: Current inventory or outstanding status, whichever the query concerns — nothing beyond that.
column6: Query closed same-visit; if not, a clear resolution timeline communicated.

column3: Who: Business Area Strength + Turnover + Scheme Tier. Where DC Stands: Upcoming to Sell (proxy) if available. Private Label: the recommended product — all three sections apply directly to this purpose.
column4: What's moving fast, what's the DC short on, any upcoming local demand (season, festival, sowing window)?
column5: The SPECIFIC product peer DCs in the same block are buying (with its Category, Business Segment, Business Category and Brand — not a generic amount); this DC's last discount on that product vs. the system-suggested discount (computed from this DC's own history + the block pattern); current stock gaps; YTD purchase and YTD PL sale so the SE can see exactly how far this DC is from its PL target.
column6: An order booked in-visit for the specific recommended product, that moves the YTD PL number — not just any SKU.
column7: S1 Block Purchase (product+category) · S2a Last Discount · S2b Suggested Discount · S3 Historical · S4 Inventory · S7 YTD Purchase · S8 YTD PL Sale

column3: Who: Business Area Strength. Where DC Stands: Upcoming to Sell (proxy) directly informs the stock alert. Private Label: not applicable.
column4: Physical stock check — what's overstocked, what's about to run out?
column5: Historical sales velocity to flag under/overstock risk; last year's stock levels at the same time for seasonal calibration.
column6: Stock discrepancies logged and a reorder trigger set for fast-moving SKUs.
column7: S3 Historical Purchase/Sale · S4 Current Inventory · S6 Last Year DC Purchase
